document.abstract: As media companies focus on growing their direct-to-consumer (D2C) businesses, the ecosystem that enables content delivery over IP-based networks continues to evolve and become even more critical. To gain efficiencies in the process, media technology providers want to better leverage each component in the content delivery path. Caching popular content at the network edge—bringing it closer to end users—is a common ISP network management practice that has long been a part of the internet’s architecture. But the new open caching standard enables a move away from proprietary systems, while still supporting an environment that leverages content delivery networks (CDNs), last mile providers, and streaming technologies that bring content closer to the consumer.

authors.bio: Sanjay Mishra is an associate fellow of Network Infrastructure Planning & Design at Verizon, Basking Ridge, NJ. He is an accomplished telecommunications professional with a background in systems development, network architecture, and design supporting both enterprise and public networks delivering video, IP, and voice services. His current focus includes the design and deployment of an edge-based technology platform for delivering streaming media within wireline and wireless networks. His other responsibilities include leadership and contributions toward the development of industry standards and technology solutions. He currently co-chairs the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) Content Delivery Networks Interconnection (CDNI) Working Group and also co-chairs the Video Immersive Study Group within the Streaming Video Technology Alliance (SVTA). He is also a Technical Fellow at SVTA.
authors.name: Sanjay Mishra

authors.bio: Erinrose Widner has been a business development leader in the M&E and technology space for over 20 years, creating transformational partnerships and innovative solutions for WB, Fox, Paramount, and ViacomCBS. She currently oversees Global Business Development for M&E, Studios and Emerging Technology for Verizon. Widely recognized as an expert in her field, she has been involved in a number of industry groups including SMPTE, HPA, WICT, NAMIC, IEEE, The Sundance Institute, Film Independent, ETC, and Women in Film. She also serves on the board of directors at Rise—a global advocacy organization supporting gender diversity across the media technology sector.
authors.name: ErinRose Widner

authors.bio: Jeff Budney’S responsibilities include peering connections to Verizon’s global internet network and developing new technology for the efficient delivery of internet content from the edge of Verizon’s ISP networks as a senior manager of network infrastructure planning. He also serves as a board member for the Streaming Video Technology Alliance, which is a global association that works to solve critical streaming video challenges in an effort to improve end-user experience and adoption. He started with Verizon Wireless in 2001 working in a variety of roles on intelligent network applications and the launch of IMS and Voice over LTE. He holds a BS in electrical engineering from Penn State, State College, PA, and an MS in electrical engineering from the Stevens Institute of Technology, Hoboken, NJ.
authors.name: Jeff Budney
